text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Swedish commercial bank Handelsbanken says the Riksbank needs to raise the repurchase rate to avoid inflation from exceeding its target over the next few years.

- Shipping company Frontline's decision to move its operations to Norway and Bermuda prompted a government investigation into how jobs can be saved by keeping shipping companies in Sweden. The Communications Ministry says some 250 jobs have been lost already and 300 more are threatened as companies seek out bases which offer lower taxes and easier labour laws.
- A bad year awaits the construction industry. Building is expected to fall sharply this year at the cost of some 15,000 jobs.

- Prime Minister Goran Persson says he will take all the necessary time to decide about Swedish participation in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU). "We don't care about the market. Working class districts and political party districts are more important this time," he says.
- Volvo Cars has placed first in a U.S. survey by JD Powers in a category called "satisfaction with overall ownership."
- More expensive fruits, vegetables and a new way of calculating the consumer price index (CPI) fuelled a 0.2 percent rise of year-on-year CPI in April.

- It will be very difficult to build an effective government if support for the Centre party continues to be as low as recent opinion polls show it is, a report by Handelsbanken shows. The Centre Party acts as the current minority Social Democratic government's informal cooperation partner.

- Telecoms group Ericsson expects to sell 50 million mobile telephone handsets over the next two years. The total market is expected to grow up to 300 million telephones by that time. The company is also planning investments totalling one billion crowns at its Kista operations north of Stockholm over the next three years.
- Riksbank Governor Urban Backstrom criticises the government's economic policies for the recent rise in debt yields and the weaker crown.

- Mail order businesses have boomed since Sweden joined the European Union, leading to several hundred new jobs. The Swedish mail order industry organisation expects Swedish mail order companies to sell as much abroad as they do at home this year.
- Norwegian car parts maker Raufoss Automotive Plastics has opened a head office in Gothenburg to be close to Swedish vehicle maker Volvo .
